headline: Senate Floor Brawl Delays UBC Vote for Third Consecutive Week
body:
The Federal Remnant's Senate chamber descended into open chaos yesterday as delegates from Axiom-aligned territories physically blocked the UBC amendment podium, delaying the Universal Basic Credits vote for the third week running. Security forces removed four delegates before order was restored. The proposed UBC program would guarantee every registered GLMZ resident a monthly floor of 1,200 quanta, funded by a contested levy on corponation operating licenses within city boundaries.

Axiom, Sterling-Nakamura, and Ironclad issued a joint statement calling the levy 'economic hostage-taking dressed as compassion,' warning of capital flight to offshore arcologies within eighteen months of implementation. Proponents, led by Senator Amara Johanssen-Liang of The Shelf delegation, counter that fourteen thousand residents in The Narrows currently survive below the 400 quanta monthly threshold. 'We are not asking for charity,' Johanssen-Liang told reporters outside the chamber. 'We are asking corponations to pay for the stability they extract from this city's bones.'

The Collective has staged sit-ins at three Axiom distribution nodes in Geartown this week, and Bore Rats operating in The Underworld reportedly intercepted and redistributed two corporate supply shipments as a demonstration of what organizers call 'pre-emptive UBC.' Iron Lotus sources, speaking anonymously, indicate the syndicate views a defeated UBC as favorable to their own micro-loan operations in The Narrows. The vote is currently scheduled for April 2nd, though procedural challenges could push it further.
aftermath: The UBC act passed in a narrow 31-29 vote on April 9th, 2131, at a reduced floor of 900 quanta monthly, triggering a two-year legal battle as Axiom filed a sovereignty-clause challenge before the Federal Remnant courts.
runner_relevance: The UBC fight spawned a dense market of political contracts almost immediately. Axiom and Sterling-Nakamura both put out courier and data-retrieval contracts to intercept Johanssen-Liang's internal communications and legislative drafts before the vote. The Collective hired runners for counter-intelligence and protection details on their organizers after two sit-in leaders were hospitalized under suspicious circumstances. Iron Lotus quietly subcontracted sabotage jobs targeting UBC registration terminals in The Shelf, aiming to suppress enrollment numbers and prove the program unworkable — paying 3,400 to 5,800 quanta per terminal.
